original_test_intent: Verify all SMBIOS Type 33 64-Bit Memory Error Information records and their error, operation, granularity, syndrome, address, resolution and device fields against the approved platform/RAS specification without generating or erasing errors.
original_method: Preserve existing RAS/SEL/OS evidence, collect complete raw Type 33 records through protected read-only access, bind them to target and time context, decode every field/sentinel and compare expected empty, unknown, stale or populated states to the owner matrix.
manual_activity: The memory/RAS owner supplies expected Type 33 presence and field semantics, staleness policy and redaction rules; an operator verifies the target and protected evidence window while automation performs read-only correlation.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/board, BIOS, SMBIOS, DIMM topology and memory configuration
Expected Type 33 record cardinality and healthy/error-state policy
Error type, granularity, operation, syndrome/vendor, address/resolution/device and sentinel semantics
Rules for stale firmware records versus current RAS/SEL/OS events
Supported dmidecode/parser version and topology/handle mapping
Protected access, physical-address redaction and evidence retention policy
safety_requirements: Do not clear dmesg, syslog, SEL, RAS or SMBIOS evidence before capture
Do not inject memory faults, reboot, alter ECC/RAS policy or reseat memory for this read-only case
Never put passwords on the command line or disable host-key verification
Capture every Type 33 record and complete stdout/stderr/status, not a heading filter
Protect physical addresses, serial/topology and vendor syndrome data under approved redaction
Do not equate absence or Unknown sentinels with health without the platform policy
Stop on stale/current ambiguity, malformed structures or topology mismatch and require RAS-owner interpretation
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, DIMM topology and Type 33 expected-state matrix
Preserve existing OS/BMC/RAS event evidence before any other action
Collect complete raw `dmidecode --type 33` through protected access
Parse every record, sentinel, error field, address, resolution and device identity
Correlate timestamps/topology with existing read-only RAS/SEL/OS evidence without inducing faults
Report comparison and preservation audit without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve healthy, empty, stale and populated Type 33 semantics
Resolve vendor syndrome, address/redaction and DIMM mapping
Determine whether a record reflects current service risk or retained history
Review evidence and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The Type 33 selector matches the source, but grep hides the actual error fields and multiple records; sshpass/disabled host checking weakens security and target identity, and source log clearing would destroy necessary correlation evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Through protected access run unfiltered `dmidecode --type 33`, retain complete output/status and existing RAS/SEL/OS logs, then decode every record against the approved topology and time-context matrix; perform no injection or clearing.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Type 33 scope, SPEC comparison, private script and 10/10-minute estimates remain; the generic clear-logs instruction is retained as source provenance but prohibited before evidence preservation.

modernized_recommendation.status: TYPE33 ERROR-STATE AND TIME-CONTEXT MATRIX REQUIRED
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Decode all 64-bit error records by handle, interpret sentinels and addresses, then correlate topology and time context with preserved RAS/SEL/OS evidence to distinguish expected absence, unknown support and retained or current faults.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds full record fields, topology/time correlation, sensitive-data protection and rejection of fault injection/log clearing.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A structure heading cannot show whether a record is empty, corrected, fatal, stale, mapped to the wrong DIMM or internally inconsistent.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: SMBIOS error records may be firmware snapshots rather than live counters; without platform lifecycle semantics they cannot alone establish current memory health.

project_override_considerations: A Project may define zero Type 33 records as expected or use a vendor RAS API for supplemental correlation, but neither may erase the source-aligned SMBIOS coverage or existing evidence. Active fault injection belongs to a separate approved testcase.
expected_evidence: SUT/BIOS/SMBIOS/DIMM/parser identity, timestamp and approved Type 33 matrix
Complete raw Type 33 stdout/stderr and exit status for every record
Parsed error type, granularity, operation, syndrome/vendor, addresses, resolution and device fields with sentinels
Topology plus stale/current/empty-state comparison against preserved RAS/SEL/OS evidence
Redaction, no-clear, no-injection and no-mutation audit
Engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target Type 33 memory-error metadata. The boilerplate clear-logs step is unsafe for evidence preservation but does not change the row's semantic target; Review explicitly prohibits it.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The Type 33 read and correlation are deterministic once expected record, topology, staleness and vendor-field semantics are supplied.

review_improvement: Retains the correct Type 33 read while adding all error fields, DIMM/time correlation, protected address evidence and an explicit ban on destroying or creating RAS evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A 64-bit error address without operation, granularity, resolution, device topology and time context can point to the wrong DIMM or an obsolete event. Conversely, no decoded record may mean healthy, unsupported or unreported. Only the complete record set plus preserved platform evidence distinguishes those states.
